lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: A semi-regular grid of high-luminance circular blobs is visible posterior to the five gill slits. The blobs are arranged in approximately four to five observable horizontal rows, with increased inter-blob spacing relative to the dense patterning on the cephalic region.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Clear vertical lines of elevated pixel intensity intersect the horizontal rows of blobs, forming a distinct checkerboard-like grid of anchor nodes across the lateral flank.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: Three primary longitudinal ridges (carinae) are visible running horizontally across the upper flank. They are defined by a high-contrast luminance gradient, with sharp white highlights on the dorsal edges and corresponding linear shadows on the ventral edges.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The visible portion of the first dorsal fin contains a high density of small, irregularly distributed high-luminance spots, primarily concentrated on the central and distal areas of the fin's surface.

other_distinctive_markers: Two small, blue-pigmented teleost fish (likely remoras) are positioned on the mid-posterior lateral flank, creating localized high-intensity blue pixel clusters against the shark's darker grey-blue skin.
